NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND AGENDA
NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
Tuesday, May 11, 2021
ONE OR MORE SUPERVISORS MAY ATTEND VIA VIDEO AND/OR TELEPHONICALLY 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors will hold a meeting open to the public on Tuesday, May 11, 2021, in the Supervisors’
Chamber in the Navajo County Governmental Complex, Holbrook, Arizona. The Board may vote to meet in a closed executive
session to discuss certain matters as indicated on the following agenda. The Board may meet in executive session pursuant
to A.R.S. § 38-431.03(A) (3) for legal advice on any item.
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors finds that it is in the best interest of the Community to conduct this public meeting using a
hybrid method in order to serve the public interest. 
Board members will participate in the meeting, in-person in the Board of Supervisors Chambers in Holbrook, or via Zoom. Limited
seating will be available for the public.  
 
To Join Zoom Meeting now, click here:  https://zoom.us/j/95679067204?pwd=bXErdHZIYzVKRGFpU3VnZ1l5ckMrUT09
Web Conference:
Call In Number: 1-669-900-6833 or 1-253-215-8782 (you may use either teleconference number)
Meeting ID: 956 7906 7204
Passcode: 404413
If you would like to speak during Call to the Public please take the following actions: 
Email Melissa Buckley at, melissa.buckley@navajocountyaz.gov 1.
Identify the Board of Supervisors' meeting date, the agenda item # and title.2.
Name & Telephone Number 3.
Comments or questions should be sent by May 10, by 5:00 pm. for the May 11, 2021, Board meeting.4.
Persons with disabilities who need accommodation to attend or participate in the meeting may contact the Clerk of the Board’s
office at (928) 524-4053; at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, so an accommodation can be arranged.
Items on the agenda may be considered out of order at the Chairman’s discretion. A copy of the agenda background material
provided to the Board, with the exception of items to be considered in executive session, is available for public inspection at Navajo
County website, www.navajocountyaz.gov 
9:00 a.m. Call To Order: Invocation and Pledge of Allegiance
           
1. CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Individuals may address the Board on any relevant issue for up to
5 minutes. At the close of the call to the public, Board members may not respond to any
comments but may respond to criticism, ask staff to review a matter or ask that a matter be
placed on a future agenda.
 
 
2. CONSENT AGENDA: These items are considered to be routine or administrative in nature
and will be approved in a single motion. A Board member may request for any item to be
removed from the consent agenda and considered on the regular agenda:
 
 
a. Minutes: April 27, 2021  
 
b. Warrant & Voucher Report over $1000 April 2021

<!-- page 2 -->
c. Constable Reports: Winslow Precinct #2, January & February 2021, Pinetop-Lakeside Precinct
#6, April 2021
 
 
d. Sympathy Letter to Honorable Wallace Youvella, Jr. and the family of Wade Carlisle  
 
e. Forest Fees Distribution amounts for School Districts 2020-21  
 
f. Tax exemptions filed pursuant to ARS §42-11153 as a Request for Redemption of Waiver  
 
g. Request for AARF funds for Show Low High School Boy's Basketball in the amount of
$1000.00
 
 
h. Contracts signed by County Manager/Assistant County Manager pursuant to Board of
Supervisors Resolution: Anasazi Medical Payment Solutions, Inc. RBR Program Services
Agreement 
 
 
i. Approval of 13 Back Tax Land Parcels sold over the counter in the amount of $6,937.60  
 
j. Resolution Number 18-2021, designating Jayson Vowell as the Navajo County Chief
Financial Officer to submit the Annual Expenditure Limitation Report for the year ended June
30, 2021
 
 
k. Resolution Number 19-2021, designating Jayson Vowell as the Navajo County Chief
Financial Officer to submit the Annual Expenditure Limitation Report for year ended June 30,
2022
 
 
l. Proclamation declaring the week of May 16 through May 22, 2021 as "National Public Works
Week" in Navajo County, Arizona and urge all citizens to show their support to our dedicated
Public Works professionals
 
 
m. Cooperative Agreement between the Holbrook Unified School District and the Navajo County
Sheriff's Office for their involvement in the School Safety Program
 
 
3. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
 
a. Update on Navajo County Fair Board Events  
Presented By: Michael Sample, NC Fair Board President
 
b. Presentation on Population Health and Quality of Life  
Presented By: Allison Hephner

<!-- page 3 -->
4. ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES:  
 
a. Introduction of the new Personnel Commission and the new Commission Chair  
Presented By: Eric Scott
 
5. SHERIFF'S OFFICE:  
 
a. Presentation and update on recent activity by the Navajo County Major Crimes Apprehension
Team (MCAT).
 
Presented By: Sheriff David Clouse 
 
6. TREASURER:  
 
a. Consideration and possible approval of a sole source agreement with HARRIS GOVERN for
Licensed Software, maintenance, and provide professional services for data conversion,
implementation, and training for a new Treasurer's System.
 
Presented By: Kari Lopez
 
7. NAVAJO COUNTY PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES DISTRICT: Board of Directors
Session: 
 
 
a. REGULAR AGENDA:  
 
1. Consideration of a Declaration of Emergency due to extreme fire danger and to enact Section
7 of County Ordinance 01-19 Emergency Fire Restrictions, to enter into Stage 1 fire
restrictions. 
 
Presented By: Catrina Jenkins
 
8. PUBLIC WORKS:  
 
a. Consideration of the award of Contract # B21-03-018 Supply and Delivery of Cattle Guards to
WW Cattle Guards, LLC.
 
Presented By: John Osgood
 
b. Consideration of Task Agreement NO. 1 to the Memorandum of Agreement between the
White Mountain Apache Tribe Division of Transportation and Navajo County that authorizes
funding assistance for replacement of road way signs and re-striping of public roads. 
 
Presented By: John Osgood

<!-- page 4 -->
9. WHITE MOUNTAIN LAKES COUNTY RECREATION IMPROVEMENT
DISTRICT: Board of Directors Session:
 
 
a. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board
wishes to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
1. Amendment No. 1 extending the Professional Services Agreement with Remarkable
Recreation Solutions for one additional year (May 26, 2021, through May 25, 2022)
 
 
10. COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE: Report from County Manager, County Attorney and
Board members.
 
 
 
11. ADJOURN  
 
Dated: May 6, 2021 NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
Posted: 3:20 p.m. By: MWB                         
Melissa W. Buckley - Clerk of the Board

Motion before the Board:
Tax exemptions filed pursuant to ARS §42-11153 as a Request for Redemption of Waiver
Background:
Background: (why should it be done, what will happen if not approved, etc. include resolution).  Pursuant to ARS
§42-11153, “If a widow, widower or disabled person whose property is exempt from tax under section §42-1111, the
person may have the waiver redeemed by the County Board of Supervisors at any regular meeting, except that no
taxes that were due and payable before the petition was submitted may be refunded or abated.” The following
applications for tax exemption were filed past the March 1 deadline, therefore, pursuant to ARS 42-11153, a “Request
for Redemption of Waiver” has been signed by each of the following:

Title: Request for AARF funds
Submitted For: Brad Carlyon, County Attorney 
Submitted By: Maxine Tyler, Executive Assistant
Department: County Attorney
Motion before the Board:
Request for AARF funds for Show Low High School Boy's Basketball in the amount of $1000.00
Background:

THE FISCAL YEAR 2021 EXPENDITURE LIMITATION REPORT TO THE AR IZONA 
AUDITOR GENERAL 
 
WHEREAS, A.R.S. §41-1279.07(E) requires each county, city, town, and community college 
district to annually provide to the Auditor General by July 31 the name of the Chief Fiscal 
Officer the governing body designated to officially submit the current year’s annual expenditure 
limitation report (AELR) on the governing body’s behalf; and 
 
WHEREAS, Entities must submit an updated form and documentation for any changes in the

officially submitting the fiscal year 2021 AELR to the Arizona Auditor General’s Office on 
the governing body’s behalf.

Navajo County 
Proclamation 
National Public Works Week 
WHEREAS, Governor Douglas A. Ducey has proclaimed May 16 -22, 2021 as National Public Works Week in 
Arizona; and 
WHEREAS, public works professionals focus on infrastructure, facilities and services that are of vital importance 
to sustainable and resilient communities and to the public health, high quality of life and well-being of the people 
of Navajo County; and 
WHEREAS, these infrastructure projects, maintenance operations, emergency management coordination and 
essential services could not be provided without the dedicated efforts of public works professionals from state 
and local governments and the private sector; and  
WHEREAS, these public works professionals are responsible for rebuilding, improving, and protecting our 
nation’s transportation system; water supply; water treatment and solid waste systems; public buildings; and other 
structures and facilities essential for our citizens; and 
WHEREAS, the men and women of  the Navajo County Public Work s, Facility Maintenance and Emergency 
Management teams excel in protecting our infrastructure and the health and safety of residents, businesses, and 
visitors by expertly providing roadway maintenance and snow removal  operations; administrative business and 
governmental finance services; facility maintenance and custodial operations; emergency management 
coordination; technical engineering and flood control services; building and zoning inspections; tribal 
transportation project and community cleanup coordination; planning and zoning services; and fleet maintenance 
operations;  and 
WHEREAS, many of our employees are emergency responders 24/7 during snowstorms, fires, floods, traffic 
accidents and other public safety incidents; and  
WHEREAS, these dedicated employees strive to embody the Navajo County values of Teamwork, 
Accountability, Integrity, Excellence, and Innovation every day while providing superior public service.  
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT PROCLAIMED, by the Board of Supervisors of Navajo County, that May 16-
May 22, 2021 is designated as “National Public Works Week” in our community and urge all the citizens of 
Navajo County to join with Governor Ducey and representatives of the American Public Works Association to 
pay tribute to the men and women of Navajo County Public Works, Facility Maintenance, and Emergency 
Management for the outstanding contributions they make in protecting our health, safety, and quality of life.  
 
PASSED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the Board of Supervisors on May 11, 2021. 
         ____________________________

Submitted For: David Clouse, Sheriff

Department: Sheriff 
Motion before the Board:
Cooperative Agreement between the Holbrook Unified School District and the Navajo County
Sheriff's Office for their involvement in the School Safety Program
Background:
The Holbrook School District has been awarded grant monies for the funding of a 10-month
School Resource Deputy's involvement and participation in their School Safety Program.  This
program and grant require certain commitments including but not limited to: 180 hours of
law-related education, full-time deputy presence on campus during school hours, weekly activity
logs, and utilization of a multidisciplinary School Safety Assessment and Prevention Team, and it
currently projected for a 3-year grant cycle. 
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2022
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested:
Fiscal Impact:
The Holbrook School District grant monies will cover all regular salary and ERE for the duration of
a 10 month period each year over a 3 year grant cycle.  Following the 10 month School Safety
Program participation period, the Deputy will return to his/her normal scheduled duties and
funding.  These funds have already been submitted as a part of the 2002 Navajo County Sheriff's
Office budget, so additional funding is not requested.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. a.        
Meeting Date: 05/11/2021  
Title: Treasurer's System
Submitted For: Kari Lopez, Treasurer  Submitted By: Kari Lopez, Treasurer
Department: Treasurer
Presented By: Kari Lopez
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and possible approval of a sole source agreement with HARRIS GOVERN for Licensed
Software, maintenance, and provide professional services for data conversion, implementation, and training
for a new Treasurer's System.
Background:
The current systems (ADT/Visions) are no longer supported and the Treasurer's Office is in jeopardy of
losing vital data if the system goes down. The Treasurer's Office and IT Department have worked with TGI
Systems, LLC on developing a Treasurer's system and after approximately 11 years are no closer to having
it completed. The Assessor's Office currently utilizes HARRIS RealWare and purchasing the HARRIS
CollectWare will reduce redundancy and increase efficiency. There are no other vendors that would be able
to provide a single "native integrated" CAMA (Assessor's System) and Treasurer's system that would utilize
the RealWare database to provide a "native integrated" CAMA and Treasurer system except for HARRIS. 
Recommendation: 
The County's Procurement Officer has determined that the Treasurer's request for sole sourcing is justified
and approved. Staff recommend approval of the agreement. 
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2021-2023
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: $800K

For optimal performance, Harris Govern requires the following hardware  specifications and

required by role: 
 
CollectWare  Database Sizing Considerations  
• Number of Parcels  
• Number of Years of Converted Data  
• Growth: 2-5% per Year  
• Versioning Drive Count is Very Imp ortant for I/O Performance  
 
File Server Sizing Considerations 
• Photos 
o Photos: 1 MB * parcel* N (keep under 1 MB for data transfer speed)  
o N is the number of photos per parcel  
▪ Example : 330,000*3*1 MB= ~1 GB for photos  
• Documents: 50 KB  
o Example : 115,000*1.5*50 KB= ~8.63 MB

1 PROJECT SUMMARY 
The COUNTY’s need is to implement a  Tax Collection system for the COUNTY staff.  CONTRACTOR will 
provide Project leadership, dedicated management, business analysis, data conversion, technical, and 
Software development services from Project inception through completion  to fulfill the COUNTY’s 
requirements as outlined in this Scope of Work (“SOW”) . The CONTRACTOR has proven experience 
leading implementation services for an organization with similar size and complexity to the COUNTY.  The 
CONTRACTOR will be expected to coordinate with the COUNTY to prepare, Configure, and implement the 
System. 
2 INTRODUCTION 
The COUNTY and the CONTRACTOR Project Team will manage Project progress by closely monitoring 
the Deliverables described in this SOW.  It is in the nature of the COUNTY, on projects of this magnitude, 
to manage the Deliverables closely as an assurance that the Project objectives, budget, and timeline will 
be met. 
A high-level Project Timeline is included in this SOW with what is known at the time of Contract execution . 
The Work for this Project will be conducted On-Site and Off-Site, as mutually determined by the COUNTY 
and the CONTRACTOR. 
3 PURPOSE 
This SOW describes the Work to be performed by the CONTRACTOR and the COUNTY including resource 
requirements, responsibilities and the Project tasks in the areas of installation, analysis, Configuration, 
development, testing, training, and Go -Live to satisfy the requirements of the Contract.  This SOW will: 
• Define the requirements of the Project so that CONTRACTOR and the COUNTY can accurately 
estimate the number of resources for each task and in turn for the overall Project.  
• Specify the various tasks to be performed and define the relationships among these t asks, to 
expose any Project risks and gaps that may span multiple tasks.  
• Outline assumptions used in pricing of the Services.  
Changes to this SOW shall follow the Change Order process  as defined in ARTICLE 47 of the Contract.

9.1.6 Communication and Documentation:  
The frequency and mode of communications regarding Project status and meeting outcomes 
(e.g. meeting notes) will be determined by the CONTRACTOR Project Manager  and

9.2 RISK MANAGEMENT 
Both COUNTY and CONTRACTOR Project Managers will manage Project risks using an agreed 
upon Project Risk Log. Project Managers will determine the best methods to manage the log . Risk 
management extends to schedule management by including the tracking of potential risks before 
they become realized issues. All Project Team members and stakeholders will communicate risks 
and determine appropriate mitigation steps.  Project risks will be discussed as part of the standing 
agenda for the Project meeting s scheduled to occur on a weekly or bi -weekly basis.  The current list 
of risks will be reviewed , and mitigation plans developed or revised as needed.  As the Project 
progresses, each Deliverable will be specifically evaluated for risk potential. Risks associated with 
each Deliverable will be identified, documented and their mitigation plans tracked until the risk period 
has effectively passed . 
9.3 ISSUE MANAGEMENT 
In the event the COUNTY Project Manager and CONTRACTOR Project Manager are unable to 
resolve an issue by partnering together, managing risk, or referencing the SOW, the Project 
Managers will adhere to SOW Section 8.2 Escalation Process .  If an issue impacts cost, scope, 
and/or schedule, the Change Order process will be followed.  If a decision has been made that does 
not require a change, it will be documented in the Project Risk Log. 
9.4 CHANGE ORDER MANAGEMENT 
The COUNTY or CONTRACTOR may in itiate a change to the project at any time. The change will 
be evaluated, and any project impact will be identified. A level of effort evaluation will be performed 
by the CONTRACTOR. The cost, scope, and schedule impact, if any, of the change, will be anal yzed 
and documented. The change impact will then be reviewed by the Executive Steering Committee for 
authorization or closure.  If the CONTRACTOR and COUNTY are unable to resolve the disposition 
of the change order, the project scope of work will remain as  defined in this SOW. 
The Parties agree that all changes must be in writing and signed by both parties.  Any change to an 
Order shall take the form of a Change Order.

The Parties agree to follow a process. In the event either Party desires to change an Order, the 
following procedures will apply:  
• The Change Order will describe the nature of the change, the reason for the change, and 
the effect the change will have on the SOW, which may include changes to Services, costs  
and the Delivery schedule . 
• The Parties will review and evaluate the proposed Change Order and negotiate in good 
faith the changes and any charges, if any, required to implement the Change Order.  If the 
Parties agree to the proposed Change Order, the Parties' authorized representa tives will 
execute the Change Order, indicating their acceptance of the changes.  
• Upon execution of the Change Order, said Change Order will be incorporated into and 
made a part of, the applicable Order.  
• A decision to move forward on any proposed Change Order will be made within five (5)  
days. 
CONTRACTOR shall under no condition perform any additional Work over the original Scope of 
Work specified in an Order without a fully executed Change Order. All requests for payment of Work 
performed under a Change Order must be accompanied by the executed Change Order. 
Whenever there is a conflict between the terms and conditions set forth in an executed Change Order 
and those set forth in the original Order or previously executed Change Order, the terms and 
conditions of the most recent executed Change Order shall control.

10.3 DATA CONVERSION 
To extract data that is required either for statutory or business purposes from the COUNTY

migrate required data from the replaced system(s) to the target System, load the data through 
automated procedures, and validate that the integrity of the data is maintained during this process .  
The CONTRACTOR’s data conversion methodology identifies all required checkpoints relating to 
a software conversion.  Each conversion st age will be executed by CONTRACTOR to ensure a 
consistent, efficient, and accurate conversion throughout the conversion stages.  The end result of 
the data conversion process will be COUNTY acceptance of its validated data in the System.

10.3.3 Preliminary Data Conversion Releases and Validation :  
The Preliminary Data Conversion is an  iterative process in which multiple releases of 
converted data will occur.  The Testing environment is configured for validation purposes.  
Any issues identified are reported and appropriate actions are taken to reconcile the issue s. 
All corrections and revisions are merged into the data conversion processes so the final data 
conversion processes will not produce similar issues.    
At least one full iteration of the Preliminary Data Conversion releases will be designed to 
emulate the exact process that will occur for Final Data Conversion.  This will serve as a trial 
or practice exercise.  
10.3.3.1  CONTRACTOR Activities:

10.3.4 Final Data Conversion:  
The Final Data Conversion is executed prior to Go -Live.  The  process occurs in four main 
steps:  
• Final Preparation and Extraction .  
• Final Conversion Program Execution .  
• Final Conversion Release. 
• Final Conversion Balancing . 
• Final Conversion Acceptance.   
During Final Preparation and Extraction, a ll necessary processes are executed on  the In-
Scope systems for final extraction.  All data entry is ceased from this point forward.  
Once final data is received, the data is validated, balanced, and integrity checks executed.  
During Final Data Conversion, the Production environment and applicable objects 
(images/documents/etc.) are transferred, installed, and configured for Go-Live purposes. In

10.7 TESTING 
CONTRACTOR follows the process depicted below for solution delivery that employs four distinct 
types of testing: Unit Testing, Regression Testing, Functional Testing, and User Acceptance Testing.  
This approach ensures the end solution provided by the CONTRACTOR satisfies all of the Fit and 
In-Scope Gap business requirements.  
10.7.1 Unit Testing:  
10.7.1.1 CONTRACTOR Activities:  
a) Code and test the Software as it is being developed and Configured to ensure 
it is meeting the functional requirements, prior to engaging the COUNTY in 
testing.  
b) Resolve defects as they arise.  
10.7.1.2 COUNTY Activities:  
a) Provide feedback on validation and edit business rules as necessary.  
10.7.1.3 Acceptance Criteria:  
a) CONTRACTOR has determined that Unit Testing outcome is successful for 
defined business functions allowing for Functional Testing and Regression 
Testing to commence. 
10.7.2 Regression Testing:  
10.7.2.1 CONTRACTOR Activities:  
a) Conduct Regression Testing of Software enhancements developed and 
System Configurations to date, ensuring the System functions as expected, 
prior to engaging the COUNTY in Functional Testing.  
b) Resolve defects as they arise.  
10.7.2.2 COUNTY Activities:  
a) Provide feedback on validation and edit business rules as necessary.  
10.7.2.3 Acceptance Criteria:  
a) CONTRACTOR determines Regression Testing outcome is successful, and 
System is ready to be deployed to COUNTY for Functional Testing.  
10.7.3 Functional Testing:  
10.7.3.1 CONTRACTOR Activities:  
a) Test all System Deliverables, including Configuration, reports, interfaces, 
enhancements, etc. prior to handing them off to the COUNTY.   
b) Provide guidance regarding the creation and management of test cases and 
the interpretation of test results.    
c) Conduct any training necessary to enable COUNTY resources to test 
effectively.

10.8 TRAINING 
All CONTRACTOR training efforts and content are designed to establish  competency in COUNTY 
staff with the System .  Training for each COUNTY role will cover all types of interactions with the 
CONTRACTOR, System  that are necessary to execute the tasks identified for that role.  
While traditional On-Site, instructor-led training remains a vital component of change management 
and knowledge transfer when implementing the System, remote and self -directed video learning 
will also be used.  A detailed Training Plan will be developed in partnership between the COUNTY 
and CONTRACTOR to ensure an optimal outcome.  For each topic and stakeholder, the 
CONTRACTOR will recommend a best pr actice training approach which might include one or 
multiple delivery methods.  
CONTRACTOR On-Site, instructor -led training sessions are typically performed at the COUNTY’s 
training facility and on the COUNTY’s hardware.  Class sizes are typically limited t o a maximum of 
fifteen (15) people in order to ensure effective participation.   
As part of t he proposed knowledge transfer and training , the CONTRACTOR will be providing 
instructor-led based on the following training areas.  
• User Acceptance  Testing Training (by functional area). 
• User Training (by functional area). 
CONTRACTOR and the COUNTY will agree to a preliminary Training Plan after kicking off the 
Project that will be further solidified by a final Training Plan post completion of the RTM.   All of the 
CONTRACTOR’s training content/materials will be specific to the curriculum and in line with the 
Software release levels the User will be using once Go -Live.  The Training P lan will be further 
modified as the Project progresses.   
Due to operational needs and staffing turnover, the CONTRACTOR agrees to : 
• Allow the COUNTY to video record the On-Site training classes for future training sessions. 
• Provide any recorded remote training sessions . 
The COUNTY can utilize those recording s, as needed, to train its staff or embed them in the help 
section of the user interface.

After review of your Sole Source Request for the HARRIS Systems USA – CollectWare, it has 
been determined that this request has been justified and is approved. The approval is based on 
the follow
ing: 
 
 The current systems ADT/Visions are no longer supported and the Treasurer’s Office is 
in jeopardy of losing vital data if the system goes down. 
 The Treasurer’s Office and the IT Department have worked with TGI Systems, LLC. on 
developing a Treasurer’s system and after approximately 11 years they are no cl oser to 
having it completed. 
 The Assessor’s Office currently utilizes RealWare which was also developed by HARRIS 
and purchasing the HARRIS CollectWare will reduce redundancy and increase efficiency. 
 There are no other vendors that would be able to provide a single “fully integrated ” 
CAMA and Treasurer system that would utilize the RealWare Database to provide a 
“fully integrated” CAMA and Treasurer system except for HARRIS. 
 
Please proceed with recommending that the Board of Supervisors approve the contract with 
HARRIS Systems USA.

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. a. 1.        
Meeting Date: 05/11/2021  
Title: Declaration of Emergency due to extreme fire danger to enact Stage 1 Fire
Restrictions
Submitted For: Catrina Jenkins, EMP Director 
Submitted By: Kellie Payton, Emergency Management Admin Asst
Department: NC Public Health Services District Division: Emergency Management
Presented By: Catrina Jenkins
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a Declaration of Emergency due to extreme fire danger and to enact Section 7 of
County Ordinance 01-19 Emergency Fire Restrictions, to enter into Stage 1 fire restrictions. 
Background:
The White Mountain Fire Coordinating Group met Monday, May 3rd to discuss the current
conditions and the possible need to enter into fire restrictions. The WMFCG is comprised of
Apache and Navajo County Emergency Management, Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest,
Arizona State Department of Forestry and Fire Management, Bureau of Land Management,
Bureau of Indian Affairs - Ft. Apache Agency, Northeast Arizona Fire Chiefs Association and
Northeast Arizona Police Association.  The primary goal of the White Mountain Fire
Coordinating Group is to create a unified approach to fire restrictions as well as information and
education. Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest will be going into Stage 1 restrictions on Friday,
May 7th, and several of the national forests in Arizona will be in restrictions soon if they are not
already.
This year we are seeing 'Extreme' and 'Extraordinary' drought conditions that have impacted the
forests throughout the entire state with significant affects in many areas. In addition to the very
dry conditions we will be seeing moderate to high Haines weather. The Haines index measures
the potential for fires to become larger and plume dominated.
 
After heavy discussion of unfavorable weather forecasts, firefighting resource availability, and
current forest conditions (including the high energy release components values and fire behavior),
it was voted unanimously to enter Stage 1 fire restrictions.  There are currently ample resources
available, however as more fires are started these resources will be called upon to help in other
regions. The current state of our land is extremely dry, and little to no relative humidity recovery
values at night. There have already been six human started fires (including an abandoned
campfire on a Red Flag day), and one naturally started lightning strike fire in just one week. If
sparks were to ignite a fire, the potential fire could be devastating. 
NCEM reminds all of our citizens and visitors that it is NEVER permissible to leave a fire
unattended or abandoned without first completely extinguishing the fire until it is cold to touch.

Staff recommends approval.

Board of Supervisors Regular 8. a.        
Meeting Date: 05/11/2021  
Title: Supply and Delivery of Cattle Guards B21-03-018
Submitted By: Stevie Studer, Account Specialist
Department: Public Works
Presented By: John Osgood
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of the award of Contract # B21-03-018 Supply and Delivery of Cattle Guards to
WW Cattle Guards, LLC.
Background:
This is a new bid and contract for two types of cattle guards used in our roadway maintenance
program - a pre-cast concrete box type used on paved County highways that carry higher volume
traffic, and a forest service standard steel frame type used on  more rural, primitive maintained
roads. As noted in the bid tab, no bids were received for the pre-cast concrete box type.  While the
County uses very few of the concrete cattle guards, staff is investigating alternative procurement
options with the state contract, ADOT and other public agencies.    Sealed proposals were
received by the Board of Supervisors at the Navajo County Government Complex, until 2:00 p.m.
M.S.T., April 28, 2021, in strict accordance with the specifications on file in the office of the
Navajo County Department of Public Works. No bids were accepted after 2:00 p.m. M.S.T. The
bids were publicly opened and read aloud at 2:15 p.m. This is a two year (multiple award) contract
for Cattle Guards. One bid was received for the standard steel frame cattle guard from WW Cattle
Guards with a decrease of $1,000.00-$2,000.00 per unit.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends award of contract # B21-03-018 Supply and Delivery of Cattle Guards to WW
Cattle Guards, LLC.

Title: WMAT-Task Agreement No 1
Submitted For: John Osgood, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Miles Begay, Engineering Tribal Trans Manager
Department: Public Works
Presented By: John Osgood
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of Task Agreement NO. 1 to the Memorandum of Agreement between the White
Mountain Apache Tribe Division of Transportation and Navajo County that authorizes funding
assistance for replacement of road way signs and re-striping of public roads. 
Background:
The White Mountain Apache Tribe Division of Transportation (WMAT DOT) and Navajo
County developed a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) that supports partnering on road
maintenance activities including supplying or transporting materials for projects; providing project
planning assistance; and assisting in road repair or maintenance activities as approved by the
Board of Supervisors.  As indicated in the attached letter, WMAT  has reached out to
Navajo County for assistance on two of their project priorities - replacing roadway
signs that have either been damaged or gone missing, and pavement
marking/striping services that will refresh pavement markers that have
deteriorated within the DOT road system. 
 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval of the attached Task Agreement between White Mountain Apache
Tribe Division of Transportation and Navajo County.

under the Arizona Constitution and related Arizona Revised Statutes. The WMAT DOT 
to fully cooperate in any audit of the Allocated Funds by the Arizona Auditor General.  
Any Allocated Funds that are unused as of June 30, 2021 shall no longer be available 
for distribution pursuant to this Memorandum of Agreement. The Allocated Funds under 
this agreement shall be paid by Navajo County directly to the invoicing party upon the 
County’s receipt of invoices or billing statement that show that the items have been 
purchased and approved by the WMAT DOT. The total of all invoices shall not exceed 
the approved amount from this agreement.
